"""Build one standalone Nxeon page: shared design system + nav + footer + the page's own body/css/js/assets."""
import json, re, base64, sys, os
MAIN = 'https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs'
GAMES = 'https://claude.ai/artifact/HMtaKgNmFhsigBQeTE9tcU'
slug = sys.argv[1]; D = f'pages/{slug}/'
meta = json.load(open(D + 'meta.json'))
p1 = open('part1.html').read(); p2 = open('part2.html').read(); p3 = open('part3.html').read()
head = re.sub(r'<title>.*?</title>', f'<title>{meta["title"]}</title>', p1, count=1)
head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', 'none').replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', 'none')
head = head.replace('</style>', open('pages/common.css').read() + open('pages/aurora.css').read() + open(D + 'page.css').read() + '</style>', 1)
sprite = p2[p2.index('<body>') + 6:p2.index('</svg>') + 6]
local = set(meta.get('anchors', []))
def fix_links(html):
    html = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith('i-')) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', html)
    return html.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"')
nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<a class="skip"'):p2.index('</header>') + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"')
nav = nav.replace('<a class="logo" href="#top"', f'<a class="logo" href="{MAIN}"')
footer = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<footer class="footer"'):p2.index('</footer>') + 9])
body = open(D + 'body.html').read()
for k, v in {'SPRITE': sprite, 'NAV': nav, 'FOOTER': footer, 'MAIN': MAIN, 'GAMES': GAMES}.items(): body = body.replace('{{' + k + '}}', v)
helpers = p3[p3.index('<script>'):p3.index('/* ------------------------------------------------------------------')]
def blk(a, b): i = p3.index(a); j = p3.index(b, i + len(a)); return p3[i:j]
js = helpers + "document.getElementById('year') && (document.getElementById('year').textContent = new Date().getFullYear());\n"
if meta.get('landmask'): js += 'const LANDMASK = "' + open('../assets/geo/mask.b64').read().strip() + '";\n'
js += blk('/* ============ Navigation ============ */', '/* ============ Reveal, rules')
js += blk('/* ============ Reveal, rules, in-view hooks, counters ============ */', '/* ============ Hero: Power Your')
js += open('pages/aurora.built.js').read() + '\n' + open(D + 'page.js').read() + "\n})();\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"
html = head + body + js
A = '../assets/'
m = {k: (v if v.startswith('/') else A + v) for k, v in meta.get('assets', {}).items()}
m.setdefault('LOGO', A + 'logo.png')
for _k in ['minecraft','rust','palworld','valheim','ark','cs2']: m.setdefault('NAV_' + _k.upper(), A + 'nav/' + _k + '.webp')
mime = lambda p: 'image/png' if p.endswith('.png') else 'image/svg+xml' if p.endswith('.svg') else 'image/jpeg' if p.endswith('.jpg') else 'image/webp'
for k in sorted(m, key=len, reverse=True):
    html = html.replace(f'__IMG_{k}__', f'data:{mime(m[k])};base64,' + base64.b64encode(open(m[k], 'rb').read()).decode())
left = set(re.findall(r'__IMG_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__', html)); assert not left, left
assert '{{' not in body, re.findall(r'\{\{[A-Z]+\}\}', body)
open(f'../dist/nxeon-{slug}.html', 'w').write(html)
open(f'test-{slug}.html', 'w').write(html.replace('<style>', '<style>@font-face{font-family:"Plus Jakarta Sans";src:url(fonts/pjs.woff2) format("woff2");font-weight:200 800;font-display:block}', 1))
print(slug, 'bytes', len(html))

Free one-click migration

Switching hosts is the worst part. So we do it for you.

One click scans your old server, detects your whole stack and brings it over installed, imported and running. No database passwords, no downtime on your old server, and it’s free.

Migrate free→How it’s different
  • Read-only on your old server
  • No DB passwords needed
  • Run it as often as you like
Nxeon migrationReady

Connect your old server

Read-only. We never store your credentials.

No agent to install. Nothing changes on this server.

0%

Migrating to nxeon-sg-01

  • Installing prerequisites
  • Copying files
  • Migrating databases
  • Starting containers
  • Verifying

Migrated and running

on nxeon-sg-01, verified live

  • Files restored to their original paths
  • MySQL and PostgreSQL databases imported
  • 3 Docker containers up with compose
  • Ports 443, 3000 and 6379 listening

We start everything we can and flag anything that needs a manual touch.

Moving from a specific host?

Step-by-step guides for the hosts people leave most.

GoDaddyHostingerBluehostDigitalOceanNamecheapHostGatorCloudwaysIONOSKamateraA2 Hosting

Before you switch

The questions everyone asks first.

Do I need my database passwords?

No. We dump MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL using root access on your old server over its local socket, so you never have to find or share database credentials.

Will my old server be affected?

No. The scan and the copy are read-only on the source. Nothing is changed, stopped or deleted, and it keeps serving traffic until you switch your DNS.

What about Docker?

We detect running containers, named volumes and Compose projects, copy the volume data and bring them back up with docker compose. Standalone containers started by hand may need a manual re-run, and we tell you which.

What if my old server runs a different OS?

We read the source OS and CPU architecture during the scan and flag differences up front, and can provision a matching OS on Nxeon.

Is it really free?

Yes. There’s no per-gigabyte fee and no migration surcharge. You only pay for the Nxeon server you keep, and you can run the migration as many times as you need.

Stop putting off the move.

Your old server keeps running the whole time. Connect it, scan it and watch your stack come up on Nxeon.

Migrate free→Have us do it for you

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

EOF

content.content:
# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**

input.message:
All four owner requests are done on staging (/nxm), not committed or deployed. There are now 28 comparison pages, including 12 new ones, and all return 200.

Screenshots are hidden by a shared regression that isn't mine: on a visitor's first page view, all /nxm pages lose their page-script widgets after load (scoreboards stay at 0, the fit quiz doesn't run, icons are missing). This includes pages that aren't mine, like /nxm/vps.
- **Cause:** the promo popup's server action sets its `nx_promo_subj` cookie, Next re-renders the route, and the page's markup is replaced after the page script has already run.
- **Status:** someone added `app/nxm/_components/StableHtml.tsx` at 12:58 to fix this, but it still reproduces for me after that. I didn't touch it.
- **My screenshots:** taken with that cookie pre-set to work around the issue. The 7-day-trial popup also covers the top of most shots.

## 1. Board animation
- **Behaviour:**
  - The server renders every cell's final characters, so with no JS or with reduced motion the board simply shows the finished text.
  - Each row flips once, the first time it is mostly in view.
  - Rows that come into view together are staggered by at most 45 ms each, capped at 500 ms in total.
  - Each character shows 3–4 random frames of 60 ms.
  - One animation loop drives every cell; there are no per-cell timers.
  - Each flip animates only transform and opacity, with no class toggling or forced reflow.
  - Cells are fixed-size and contained, so swapping a character never re-lays out the board.
  - Columns that are hidden on phones aren't animated.
- **Measured with Playwright:** about 0.6 s on desktop (≈650 character swaps across the rows in view) and about 0.45 s on a phone (≈110 swaps). The design's version took several seconds.
- **Where:** the design's flap script is replaced in `tools/nxm/wire/compare.py`.

## 2. Readable FROM column
- FROM is no longer split-flap glyphs: it shows the logo and the plain company name in normal type (600 weight, light text). The flap look stays on the time, destination and "you gain" columns.
- On phones the time column is now hidden so the name has room; it is untruncated at 390 px.
- **Additions:**
  - A filter above the board: All routes / Cloud and VPS / Game servers.
  - The boarding pass's baggage line and check-in button follow the row. Game hosts show "Your world files / Full file access" and link to /game-servers instead of migration, because the SSH migration doesn't apply to game hosts.

## 3. Logos
Shown in the FROM column and on each comparison page's hero plate. The logo module is `app/nxm/_data/vs-logos.ts`: a file is only used if it has a manifest entry with its source URL and the date checked (2026-09-27).
- **Simple Icons (light single colour on the dark page):** DigitalOcean, Hostinger, GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudways, IONOS, Hetzner, Contabo, Vultr, OVH, AWS, BisectHosting.
  - Linode uses the Akamai glyph, because linode.com itself now shows the Akamai logo.
- **Official files** in `public/nxm/logos/competitors/`, each downloaded once from the company's own site and sized only:
  - aternos.png, shockbyte.png, apexhosting.svg, ggservers.png, hosthavoc.svg, dathost.png, ultahost.png, sparkedhost.png, gportal.png, nitrado.png, pebblehost.png.
  - PebbleHost only publishes a combined logo, so I kept the icon and dropped the wordmark beside it, since the page already prints the name. That's the one edit beyond sizing.
- **No logo, name only:**
  - Bluehost, HostGator and Kamatera: their sites return 403 to every request from this server.
  - A2 Hosting: a2hosting.com now redirects to hosting.com (a rebrand), so there is no A2 mark to take.
  - To add one: drop the official file in the folder and add a manifest entry.

## 4. New comparisons (12 routes)
Routes: `/aternos-alternative`, `/shockbyte-alternative`, `/apexhosting-alternative`, `/ggservers-alternative`, `/hosthavoc-alternative`, `/dathost-alternative`, `/sparkedhost-alternative`, `/gportal-alternative`, `/bisecthosting-alternative`, `/nitrado-alternative`, `/pebblehost-alternative`, `/ultahost-alternative`.

- **Built on the same template**, with registry entries (title, description, canonical, "X alternative" breadcrumb) and a row each on /compare.
- **Structured data:** breadcrumbs, FAQPage (5–6 questions), and Product offers. Game hosts get Minecraft tiers as the offers; UltaHost gets VPS plans.
- **Competitor facts:** one constant per competitor in `app/nxm/_data/vs-hosts-data.ts`. Every figure carries its source page and "checked 2026-09-27", which is also printed on the page.
  - Research was done by four subagents using only each company's own site.
  - I re-read every price myself from the raw page HTML, or with one headless-browser page load for Nitrado.
  - That re-check caught one research error: GGServers' two prices are Standard vs Premium location prices, not intro vs renewal. It is corrected.
- **Nxeon's side is read from the system on every request:** Minecraft tiers and slots, VPS plans, games count, regions, free Minecraft tier setting, one-click mod support, backup retention, support promise, the Terms' "fees are non-refundable", and the annual discount.
- **Price rows** compare their plan against Nxeon's plan with the same RAM. The verdict is computed from the numbers (±3% counts as even).
- **UltaHost** is compared with Nxeon on the same 24-month term, because its advertised prices require a 24-month prepay.
- **No migration claims:** game-host pages drop the migration section (game hosts don't give SSH access).

| Host | Figures used (source page) |
|---|---|
| Aternos | Free forever, queue, stops when last player leaves, unlimited slots, backups to Google Drive (aternos.org, support.aternos.org) |
| Shockbyte | Sand / Iron / Emerald $5.59 / $11.19 / $22.39 (30% off recurring), 60+ games, 8 locations, 72-hour refund, 24/7 support, 50% off annually (shockbyte.com pages, /api/locations, terms) |
| Apex Hosting | 4 GB / 8 GB $14.99 / $27.99 recurring (first month $8.99 / $16.79), 28 games listed, 14 locations, 7-day refund, 300 Gbps DDoS protection |
| GGServers | $6 / $12 / $24 in Standard locations, double in Premium, SSD storage, 24-hour first-order refund |
| Host Havoc | $10 / $20 / $40 regular (currently 25% off), 14 locations, 72-hour money-back |
| DatHost | Prices are in euros only (€14.90 for one 16 GB plan), so there is no price verdict; 49 cities, 14-day refund |
| Sparked Host | Budget line $2 / $4 / $8, backups a paid add-on, 48-hour refund, 24-hour free trial |
| GPORTAL | $6.14 / $13.43 per 30 days (25% off the first period only), 100 games, 12 regions |
| BisectHosting | No price rows: its price table only loads in the browser; 110+ games, 21 locations, 72-hour refund, 7 days of backups |
| Nitrado | 2 GB with 10 slots $16.19 per 30 days (read with one headless browser load), 100+ games, 9 locations, 3–365-day rentals |
| PebbleHost | Budget 4 GB / 8 GB $4 / $8, 72-hour refund, 480 Gbps DDoS protection |
| UltaHost | VPS Business / Professional $9.78 / $15.87 on a 24-month term, 27+ data centers, 30-day refund (2- and 3-year plans excluded) |

## Owner decisions
1. **Several honest game-host pages show Nxeon winning zero rows on staging:** DatHost, BisectHosting and PebbleHost. Competitors win on locations, refunds, 24/7 support and unlimited slots. On staging, Nxeon wins every Minecraft price row against Shockbyte; production tiers are pricier, so some of those verdicts flip there. Decide whether to publish these as they are.
2. **Gaps you could fill:**
   - Refund terms and support hours for Nitrado.
   - Server locations for Aternos.
   - BisectHosting's price table.
3. **Staleness:** competitor prices and promotions (the "30% off recurring", "25% off" and promo-code prices) need a re-check before launch.
4. **More regions coming:** the old fail-closed region check was changed to a warning by someone else. Pages still print "Singapore and Germany" from the system, but the live comparison text for the original 16 still hard-codes two regions.

## Files
- **New:**
  - `app/nxm/_data/vs-hosts.ts` (Nxeon system values and the builder)
  - `app/nxm/_data/vs-hosts-data.ts` (competitor constants)
  - `app/nxm/_data/vs-logos.ts` (logo manifest)
  - `public/nxm/logos/competitors/*` (11 files)
- **Updated:**
  - `app/nxm/_data/vs-competitors.ts`
  - `app/nxm/_data/vps-vs-digitalocean.ts`
  - `app/nxm/_data/compare.ts`
  - `tools/nxm/wire/vps_vs_digitalocean.py` (hero logo slot; migration section only for cloud hosts; closing button slot)
  - `tools/nxm/wire/compare.py`
  - `tools/nxm/native/vps-vs-digitalocean/body.html`
  - `tools/nxm/routes/vps-vs-digitalocean.json` (now 28 routes)
  - `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (12 entries added)
- The typecheck is clean for all my files.

content.text:
All four of the owner's /compare changes are done on staging under /nxm. That includes 12 new game-host and VPS comparisons, so there are now 28 comparison pages and all load. Nothing is committed or deployed.

**Before you look at the pages:** on a visitor's first visit, every /nxm page loses its interactive parts right after it loads. Scoreboards stay at 0, the "which is right for you" quiz doesn't work and icons are missing. This hits pages that aren't mine too, such as /nxm/vps.
- **Cause:** the 7-day-trial popup sets a visitor cookie on the first visit, which makes Next reload the page content and wipe what the page script built.
- **Status:** someone added a fix (`app/nxm/_components/StableHtml.tsx`) at 12:58. It still happens for me after that, and I didn't touch it.
- **Screenshots:** I took mine with that cookie pre-set to get around it. The popup still covers the top of most of them.

**1. Board animation.** It now plays once and takes about 0.6 s on desktop and 0.45 s on a phone, measured in a real browser. The old version ran for several seconds.
- Each row flips once, the first time it comes into view. Rows that appear together are staggered and each character shows only 3–4 random frames.
- One animation loop drives every character, and each flip moves only transform and opacity, so it never forces layout work.
- With reduced motion, or without JavaScript, the finished board simply shows.

**2. Readable names.** The company column now shows the logo and the plain name in normal type, with no flap. The flap look stays on the time, destination and "you gain" columns.
- On phones I hid the time column so names aren't cut off at 390 px.
- I also added a filter above the board: All routes / Cloud and VPS / Game servers.
- For game hosts, the boarding pass now points to game servers instead of free migration. That migration works over SSH, and game hosts don't give SSH access.

**3. Logos.** They appear in the board and on each comparison page's hero.
- **Simple Icons** covers 12 brands. Linode uses the Akamai mark, because linode.com itself now shows it.
- **Official icons** for 11 hosts were downloaded once from their own sites into `public/nxm/logos/competitors/`. Each has its source URL and date in `app/nxm/_data/vs-logos.ts`, and a file without a manifest entry is ignored.
- **PebbleHost:** it only publishes a combined logo, so I kept the icon and dropped the wordmark beside it. That's the one edit beyond resizing.
- **Name only, no logo:**
  - Bluehost, HostGator and Kamatera block every request from this server.
  - a2hosting.com now redirects to hosting.com, so there is no A2 Hosting logo to take.

**4. New comparisons.** Aternos, Shockbyte, Apex Hosting, GGServers, Host Havoc, DatHost, Sparked Host, GPORTAL, BisectHosting, Nitrado, PebbleHost and UltaHost, each at `/<name>-alternative`. I added Sparked Host and GPORTAL myself.
- **Each page has:** title, description, canonical, breadcrumbs, FAQ and product structured data, a registry entry and a row on /compare.
- **Sourcing:** every competitor figure is from that company's own site, stored in one constant per competitor in `app/nxm/_data/vs-hosts-data.ts`, with its source page and "checked 2026-09-27" shown on the page.
- **Verified prices:** I re-read every price myself. That caught one research error: GGServers' two prices are Standard vs Premium location prices, not intro vs renewal. It's corrected.
- **Nxeon's side:** read from the system on every request, including Minecraft tiers, VPS plans, games, regions, backups, support promise, the Terms' no-refund clause and the annual discount.
- **Price comparisons:** each row compares plans with the same RAM, and the verdict is computed from the numbers.
  - UltaHost's advertised prices require a 24-month prepay, so it is compared against Nxeon's own 24-month price.
  - DatHost only prices in euros, so it gets no price verdict. I didn't convert currencies.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Publish as is?** On staging, the DatHost, BisectHosting and PebbleHost pages show Nxeon winning zero rows. The competitors honestly win on locations, refund windows, 24/7 support and unlimited player slots. Against Shockbyte, Nxeon wins every Minecraft price row on staging, but production prices are higher, so some of those verdicts flip there.
2. **Missing facts:** I couldn't source Nitrado's refund terms and support hours, Aternos's server locations, or BisectHosting's price table (it only loads in a browser). Those rows are simply absent.
3. **Re-check before launch:** competitor promotions change often ("30% off recurring", "25% off", a promo-code price).
4. **More regions:** someone changed my region check from blocking the page to only logging a warning. The live comparison text on the original 16 pages still says "two regions" in its prose.
